properties.decision:
DECIDED by Anthony 2026-08-04, taking the split this node had already written down while it was open: CLAIMS IN THE GRAPH for who has what, COORD.md RETAINED for the conventions and the merge-conflict doctrine, and the IN-PROGRESS TABLE DELETED rather than maintained in two places — because two places for the same fact is the failure the whole documents-into-the-graph move exists to end.

THE STATED BLOCKER DISSOLVED RATHER THAN BEING OVERRULED, which is worth recording precisely because this node held itself open on it since 2026-07-25. The rationale read: "a claim board is a coordination mechanism between two people, and switching it unilaterally would mean one of them silently changing where the other must look; that is Anthony's brother's call as much as his." Anthony, 2026-08-04: "my brother hasn't actively developed any of this apart from offering feedback." So there is no second writer to strand — the premise was that two people coordinate through this board, and only one of them has ever written to it. The caution was correct when written and the fact it was resting on turned out not to hold. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NARROWER THAN THE DECISION LOOKS: reflow2 still has no live multi-writer case, so the claims layer remains UNPROVEN under contention. This move proves it under a single writer only, and that limit should not be quietly forgotten the first time a second person appears.

⭐ THE PREREQUISITE WAS RUN, AND IT PASSED ON A CAPABILITY THE MARKDOWN STRUCTURALLY CANNOT HAVE. This node named its own gate — "nobody has used claim_region for real yet, so the first move is to run it on one real piece of work and see whether claim_report says something a person would have said." Run 2026-08-04 on the live work: `claim_region` with seed `cap:corpus-ingest`, depth 2, contributor `who:ajs`, carrying BL-186's note. `claim_report` returned the claim, zero overlaps, zero stale — and `liveness: "live"`, COMPUTED from the claiming seat's host and pid rather than stored. Its own advisory states the payoff: "`gone` means that session has exited and the claim is a ghost (excluded from overlaps), `unknown` means it was made on another machine or before seats were recorded — unknown is never read as free, because taking work somebody is actively doing is the expensive mistake."

THAT IS THE DIRECT FIX FOR THE FAILURE THAT PROMPTED THIS, and it is not the reason first given. This node argued the gain was that a computed region FOLLOWS THE DESIGN instead of going stale as a hand-typed file list. True, but secondary. The measured failure is different: on 2026-08-04 COORD.md was carrying BL-186 as in-progress after #73 had landed it, and the file itself contains a note recording that this was the THIRD STALE CLAIM FOUND IN ONE SWEEP. A markdown line cannot know its author walked away — a claim is only ever retired by someone remembering to retire it, which is exactly the class of thing people forget. Liveness computed from the session means an abandoned claim reads `gone` on its own, with nobody remembering anything. The markdown board was not merely going stale; IT HAD NO MECHANISM BY WHICH IT COULD EVER NOT.

WHAT IS KNOWINGLY GIVEN UP, restated at the point of deciding rather than left in the open-question text where it would read as unresolved: COORD.md's in-progress table was readable by a human with no reflow2 and no binary, and it appeared as a diff in every pull request. A graph claim does neither — it travels in the committed export, so it is visible, but reading it needs the tool. That is accepted deliberately. The conventions, the handles table and the merge-conflict doctrine STAY in COORD.md for exactly that reason: they are addressed to someone who may not have reflow2 running, and they are prose about practice rather than facts about state.

THE STANDING RULE THIS SETS, and it is the general form: A DOCUMENT SHOULD HOLD WHAT IS ADDRESSED TO SOMEONE WITHOUT THE TOOL, AND THE GRAPH SHOULD HOLD WHAT THE TOOL CAN COMPUTE. COORD.md splits cleanly along that line — practice stays, state goes. It is the same test as `dec:the-transition-is-two-halves-and-reads-are-the-unscheduled-one` ("can you delete this document and regenerate it from the graph?"), and the in-progress table is the first thing in this repo to pass it by being deleted rather than by already having been derived.
properties.name: DECIDED — the claim board moves into the graph; COORD.md keeps the conventions and the conflict doctrine
properties.rationale:
Raised as a dogfooding question, which is how most of this project's real findings have arrived — and it was a genuinely good test of the claims layer.

MOVED TO ACCEPTED 2026-08-04 on Anthony's explicit word, after its own stated prerequisite was run for the first time. Two things are recorded here that a later reader would otherwise have to reconstruct. FIRST, the decision did not overrule its objection — the objection's premise (two people coordinating) turned out to be false, and saying so is different from deciding against it, because if a second writer ever appears the caution becomes live again rather than having been settled. SECOND, the reason for the move is not the reason originally given: computed-region-follows-the-design was the argument, and computed LIVENESS turned out to be what actually fixes the observed failure. The original argument was not wrong, it was aimed at the wrong half — worth keeping, because it is the second time in this project a fork resolved on something outside the recorded options (see the method finding on dec:agent-navigates-content).

The unproven-under-contention limit is stated on the node rather than left implicit: a single-writer proof is what was obtained, and the claims layer's real case is still ahead of it.
